issue.title: keycloak.policy-enforcer doesn't take effect when setting root context path in a certain pattern

labels.name: triage/duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
I turn on keycloak security authorization for my api and turn it off for *public* apis including:
- metrics
- openapi
- health
I can access public apis as expected, however, when I set my `quarkus.http.root-path` to `/api/workbench`, I always get `401 unauthorized error` when accessing public apis

Please note: from my observations this bug **only** apply to root context path `/api/workbench`.
It works with other paths such as:
- /api
- /api/work
- /api/workwork2

I tested both in my application and in [quarkus quickstart](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-quickstarts)

**Expected behavior**
I should access to public API


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1.  clone from [security-keycloak-authorization-quickstart](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-quickstarts/tree/master/security-keycloak-authorization-quickstart)
2. remove public api java code: `PublicResource.java` 
3. add dependencies:
```
    <dependency>
      <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
      <artifactId>quarkus-smallrye-opentracing</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
      <artifactId>quarkus-smallrye-openapi</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
      <artifactId>quarkus-smallrye-metrics</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
      <artifactId>quarkus-smallrye-health</artifactId>
    </dependency>
```

**Configuration**
```properties
# OIDC Configuration
quarkus.oidc.auth-server-url=some-url
quarkus.oidc.client-id=backend-service
quarkus.oidc.credentials.secret=secret
quarkus.http.cors=true

# Enable Policy Enforcement
quarkus.keycloak.policy-enforcer.enable=true

quarkus.keycloak.policy-enforcer.paths.1.path=/api/workbench/public/*
quarkus.keycloak.policy-enforcer.paths.1.enforcement-mode=DISABLED

quarkus.http.root-path=/api/workbench
quarkus.smallrye-openapi.path=/public/openapi
quarkus.swagger-ui.path=/public/swagger-ui
quarkus.smallrye-health.root-path=/public/health
```

**Environment:**
 - quarkus version:
Quarkus 1.3.0.final
 - Output of `java -version`: 
`openjdk version "13" 2019-09-17
OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 13+33)
OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM (build 13+33, mixed mode, sharing)`

body:
This is probably most relevant, what Pedro commented at #8204 :
```
If you run the application in dev mode, the paths you defined to the policy enforcer (e.g.: quarkus.keycloak.policy-enforcer.paths.1.path=/swagger-ui/*) is not loaded and that causes the policy enforcer to deny the request.
```

issue.title: Disabled keycloak.policy-enforcer.paths is not publicly accessible

labels.name: triage/duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

issue.body:
I tried to run the [keycloak-authorization example](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/tree/master/integration-tests/keycloak-authorization) from the quarkus repository. The policy enforcer config is as follows:

```
# Enable Policy Enforcement
quarkus.keycloak.policy-enforcer.enable=true
quarkus.keycloak.policy-enforcer.enforcement-mode=ENFORCING
-----
-----
# Disables policy enforcement for a path
quarkus.keycloak.policy-enforcer.paths.4.path=/api/public
quarkus.keycloak.policy-enforcer.paths.4.enforcement-mode=DISABLED
```

When I tried to access /api/public without any authorization, it is showing 401 Unauthorized error. So my question is whether this is an expected behavior? From what I have understood, since enforcement-mode is set to DISABLED, the API should be accessible by public without any authorization. I need to build some APIs which should be publicly available. How can I get this behaviour?

Also when I repeatedly access this api, I get "java.lang.IllegalStateException: Request has already been read" time to time.

body: Thank you! I tried to implement this last week and wasn't sure what I was doing wrong. I can confirm it works as expected in `1.4.1`, so it must have been introduced in `1.4.2`.
As observed by @garmannslund, it's working for me too in 1.4.1, but not in 1.4.2.
